A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Rethinking Losses for Diffusion Bridge Samplers. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, appendices and checklists are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original diffusion-sampler experiments in Section 5, Figure 1 and Tables 1–3, with additional 100-dimensional benchmark results in Appendix B, Tables 4–5.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their results in Section 5 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The rKL-LD objective, gradient estimators, CMCD/DBS parameterizations and Algorithms 1–3 are unchanged. Although revised Section 3.3 mentions adaptation across time, Section 5 and Appendix D.3 still specify time-constant diffusion coefficients and leave time-dependent schedules to future work.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Seeds, Sonar, Credit, Brownian and LGCP, plus Funnel, Many Well, and GMM-40 and MoS-10 targets in 50 and 100 dimensions. The higher-dimensional experiments already appear in v2 Appendix B.

E2.justification: Each corresponding comparison retains the same CMCD and DBS variants trained with rKL-R, LV and rKL-LD, with the same learned/fixed diffusion-coefficient variants. Table 5 retains its fixed-coefficient-only comparator set.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendices C–D retain the training budgets, 128 diffusion steps, batch sizes, grid searches, checkpoint-selection rules, metrics and evaluation sample counts. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: Figure 1 and its analysis retain the Brownian learned-versus-fixed coefficient comparison, dimensional coefficient profile, uniform-average coefficient control and Seeds initialization-sensitivity experiment. No ablation or robustness analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Appendix D.1 retains the three-seed standard-error reporting and the seven-seed, 30-repetition protocol specified for the 50-dimensional mixtures. Figure 1 retains its standard deviations across three independent seeds.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 match, including uncertainties and divergence markers. Figure 1, the data-processing counterexample plot and the reported empirical findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 removes the entire formal entropy argument supporting diffusion-coefficient learning: Section 3.3's marginal-to-joint entropy bound and joint-entropy formula, v2 Equations 14–15, and Appendix A.5's derivation. This substantially reduces the theoretical justification for that component. The gradient derivations and continuous/discrete data-processing counterexamples remain, with the latter renumbered from A.6 to A.5.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about LV gradient inequivalence, its failure of data processing, rKL-LD's performance and stability, and benefits from learning diffusion coefficients.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 replaces the claimed entropy requirement for covering the target distribution with a qualitative explanation involving exploration, coverage and excessive noise. It adds discussion of restricted exploration and slower convergence. The empirical interpretations and Section 6 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D retains the same architecture, parameterizations, optimizer, clipping, learning-rate schedule, hyperparameter grids and pseudocode. The code-access statement and configuration-directory instructions are unchanged.

R1.justification: The Shannon (1948) citation and bibliography entry are removed with the entropy argument. The remaining citations and positioning relative to diffusion samplers, diffusion bridges and GFlowNets are unchanged.

P1.justification: The substantive prose rewriting is concentrated in Section 3.3. Removing the entropy appendix also changes subsection numbering and cross-references, while the overall narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 and the main tables shift vertically; Table 3 now sits beside the ablation discussion rather than the benchmark description. The pseudocode occupies a separate page before the checklist, and other material reflows. Figures, table structures and captions are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 removes a localized mathematical overstatement: for the continuous variables used here, the chain rule does not guarantee v2 Equation 14's entropy bound because conditional differential entropy can be negative. Replacing the associated necessity claim with qualitative motivation improves rigor. Although no replacement formal guarantee is supplied, the method, empirical support and central theoretical results are preserved.
